traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Eriophyllum lanatum: stems (from 10 cm) 20 cm to 60 cm tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Eriophyllum lanatum: leaves 2 cm to 6 cm long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low, woolly, grey herb of many stems with small lobed leaves and bright yellow daisy heads. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.4 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: silvery grey-green leaves; yellow heads.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Eriophyllum lanatum (pp. 225-226): stems (1)2-6 dm; var. grandiflorum 3-10 dm, and the generic key gives the perennials 1-10(15) dm.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): erect or sprawling from a woody base; the key calls it shrubby only at the base.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): lower leaves spatulate or oblanceolate, stem leaves oblong-lanceolate to obovate, uppermost narrow.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): one blade, entire to pinnatifid.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): lower leaves entire or lobed, stem leaves pinnatifid, uppermost usually entire; var. achillaeoides pinnately to tripinnately divided.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): pinnatifid.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): once pinnatifid in the type; up to three times in var. achillaeoides.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, varieties of E. lanatum (p. 226): segments and narrow leaves entire; several varieties coarsely serrate or toothed.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): heads solitary or loosely corymbose on peduncles 5-10 cm long.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): rayed; rays lacking only in var. aphanactis.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): involucre hemispheric, 8-10 mm high; 5-12 mm across the varieties.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): involucre 10-12 mm broad; heads 1.5-3 cm across with rays (key).

traits.phyllaries.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): phyllaries 8-12, keeled, free with overlapping margins.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): ray florets 8-12.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): rays 10-20 mm; 6-10 mm in several varieties.

traits.ray_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): rays yellow. Word: yellow.

traits.pappus.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): pappus of 4-10 blunt erose scales; in var. arachnoideum reduced to a crown of teeth.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (pp. 225-226): achenes 3-4 mm long; 2-5 mm across the varieties.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. lanatum (p. 225): May to July.
